events.title: Mozilla source code open-sourced
events.summary: On March 31, 1998, Netscape released the Mozilla browser suite source code under an open license — the foundation for Firefox, Thunderbird, and modern Gecko engines.
events.about: The Mozilla project turned Netscape's codebase into a community effort after AOL acquired the company. Out of years of rewrite came Gecko, Firefox, and a proof that open-source browsers could compete with billion-dollar platforms.

narrative.whyChosen: Mozilla open source is the direct ancestor of Firefox and the modern open-web browser movement.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept an independent browser engine alive when Netscape as a product company faded.
narrative.problemSolved: Netscape needed outside developers to help finish a modern browser rewrite it could not fund alone.
